chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man divorces his wife while he is absent, and she does not know of it until a year or more or less has passed, then when she learns of it, she marries (another man) and does not observe the waiting period (Iddah). And if her husband dies while he is absent, she observes the waiting period from the day the news reaches her, even if he had died a year or two before that.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman's waiting period (Iddah) when her husband is absent and she learns of his divorce or death later?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the practical application of Iddah for absent husbands, distinguishing between divorce and death by anchoring the waiting period to the receipt of news rather than the actual event. This ruling, found in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, addresses the uncertainty of time in pre-modern communication, ensuring legal certainty for remarriage. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the 'known' event (news arrival) triggers the obligation, preventing indefinite limbo for the woman.
